clue.text: Cigar making flawless ring…

parts.note: something flawless is perfect, without any fault
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cigar maker produces a perfect smoke ring, and the sentence trails off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word. The ellipsis carries the clue on into 5-across, where the word 'Cigar' is reused.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecto is a type of cigar that is thick in the middle and tapers at both ends.

clue.text: Lamps put out for this sacred song?

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or disordered, so the letters of lamps are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lamps are switched off for a hymn in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a hymn from the Old Testament Book of Psalms, sung in worship.

clue.text: Try early, without the relevant facts

definitions.text: Try early, without the relevant facts

parts.words: Try early, without the relevant facts
parts.note: try in the sense of judge a case, done in advance before the evidence is heard

explanation.surface: A court rushes a trial before the evidence is in.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as FORE (early) and JUDGE (try), but the whole clue describes judging in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To forejudge is to prejudge, deciding a matter before hearing the evidence.

clue.text: One struck with hammers by a bar counter?

definitions.text: One struck with hammers by a bar counter?

parts.words: One struck with hammers by a bar counter?
parts.note: a keyboard instrument whose hammers hit metal bars, read as if it were a drunk hit at a pub counter

explanation.surface: Someone gets hit with hammers near the counter of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar counter' suggests a pub; in fact the instrument counts out its notes on bars, being struck by hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a small keyboard instrument in which hammers strike steel plates, giving a bell-like tone.

clue.text: Proudly sitting up

parts.note: a haughty, superior manner, pictured literally as being seated up high on a tall mount

explanation.surface: Someone sits up straight with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means acting in an arrogant, superior way.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for behaving arrogantly or self-righteously, as if mounted above others.

clue.text: …rejected, after a short time — that's sad

indicators.note: after puts the turned-round word behind the short time

parts.note: T is the usual abbreviation for time, a time cut short

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the cigar from the clue before is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: the word Cigar is carried over from the opening of 1-across by the ellipsis

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-across, the cigar is thrown away after a brief moment, which is a sorry business.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 1-across: the thing 'rejected' is the word 'Cigar' from that clue, and 'rejected' turns it into RAGIC, which follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic and sad are near synonyms, both describing something that causes sorrow or grief.

clue.text: Forbidden to take half dollar, horizontally flattened

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden

indicators.note: half here takes the second three letters of the six-letter word dollar

explanation.surface: Banned from accepting fifty cents, someone is squashed flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link word. 'half' takes LAR, the back half of DOLLAR, not the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabular means shaped like a table, having a broad flat top.

clue.text: Got idea for re-potting plant

indicators.note: re-potting means moving into a new pot, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener has a bright idea about repotting a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is a flowering garden annual, a genus of showy plants.

clue.text: Clarence collecting some mail after eviction

annotationWithheld.why: Clarence collecting some mail after eviction (9) for CLEARANCE: CLARENCE plus A cannot give CLEARANCE by insertion (the E and A are out of order), and no search found a different printed clue or an accepted parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: Clarence collecting some mail after eviction

clue.text: Morning examination is unethical

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, the hours of morning
an oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test

explanation.surface: Someone thinks setting an exam in the morning is immoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amoral lacks any moral sense, so their behaviour is without ethics.

clue.text: Lower link in a privileged education

parts.note: a lower is something that lows or moos, so an ox, not something further down
a bridge links two places together

explanation.surface: A link further down the social ladder enters an elite schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like the opposite of higher, but read it as 'one that lows' (moos): cattle low, so it is OX. OXBRIDGE means Oxford and Cambridge universities together.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge are Britain's oldest and most prestigious universities, so studying there is a byword for a privileged schooling.

clue.text: Appropriate term for dust particle, only now stuck inside

indicators.note: stuck inside means one piece is lodged within the other

parts.note: a mote is a speck of dust
just means only now, as in 'he has just arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for the right word for a speck of dust that has only now become lodged.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT JUSTE is French, used in English for exactly the right word.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing meaning the exactly right word or expression for the occasion.

clue.text: Refuse of a young family

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun is rubbish dropped carelessly
a brood of newborn animals, such as puppies or kittens, born together

explanation.surface: Rubbish left behind by a family with small children.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rubbish strewn about and a set of animals born to one mother at one time.

clue.text: Garden feature not only for dippers and divers

definitions.text: Garden feature not only for dippers and divers

parts.words: Garden feature not only for dippers and divers
parts.note: dippers and divers are both kinds of bird, so the feature is one where birds splash about, not people swimming

explanation.surface: A garden pond seems meant for people who dip and dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Dippers and divers sound like swimmers, but both are bird names.
explanation.definitionFit: A small basin of water in a garden where birds drink and wash.

clue.text: Number in Venice?

parts.note: a number is a song or piece of music, here one sung on the canals of that Italian city

explanation.surface: A question about a figure or quantity in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure; it is a musical number, the song of the gondoliers.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a boating song traditionally sung by Venetian gondoliers.

clue.text: Georgia, in check, has to recover

indicators.note: in places the US state's abbreviation inside the word for check

parts.note: a rein checks or restrains, as in 'rein in spending'
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Georgia, held back, must get something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to get it back after losing it.

clue.text: Heroism shown by everybody inside rocket-launching tower

indicators.note: inside puts the word for everybody within the tower

parts.note: a gantry is the framework tower beside a rocket on its launch pad
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Bravery is displayed by everyone working in a launch tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is bravery, especially courage in battle, as recognised by gallantry medals.

clue.text: Modern centre spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of centre are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A centre spread in a modern magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recent belongs to the present or the near past, so it is new and up to date.

clue.text: What may be pushed back in digital display?

definitions.text: What may be pushed back in digital display?

parts.words: What may be pushed back in digital display?
parts.note: digital refers to fingers, so this is the skin at the base of a fingernail, pushed back in a manicure

explanation.surface: A question about something retreating on a digital screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital display' suggests electronics; digital here means of the fingers (digits).
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the strip of hardened skin at the base of a nail, often pushed back in manicure.

clue.text: Half of them, split asunder, have survived

indicators.note: half of takes the first two letters of the four-letter word them

parts.note: riven means torn or split apart

explanation.surface: Half of a group, though broken apart, have lived on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' is a link word: 'have thriven' means 'have survived'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriven is the past participle of thrive, to flourish or prosper and so to have come through.

clue.text: Spirit of us motorists so genial, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters turn and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: American drivers prove to be so friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the United States: GASOLINE is the American word for petrol, and 'spirit' is an old word for motor fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is motor spirit, and Americans call that fuel by this name, often shortened to gas.

clue.text: Those unmarried southern English people in Spain

parts.note: in Spain the word for English, or an English person, is inglés, written here without its accent

explanation.surface: Unmarried English people from the south living in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Spain' signals a Spanish word: the Spanish for English is inglés.
explanation.definitionFit: Singles are people who are not in a couple or married.

clue.text: Creator of a universal god

parts.note: U is the British film rating meaning universal, suitable for everyone
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A maker of a god worshipped everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is the originator or maker of something, not only a writer of books.

clue.text: Do in a battery?

parts.note: a do is a party, and battery farms keep laying birds in cages, so it is a party for those birds

explanation.surface: A question about what happens inside an electric battery.
explanation.walkthrough: A HEN PARTY is a celebration held by a bride-to-be and her female friends before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration for a bride and her friends, punning on the hens kept in battery cages.

clue.text: Constituent of some drink, as in still?

indicators.note: in places the word as inside the word for still

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not done yet'
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ingredient of a drink, as found in a distillery still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like the distilling apparatus, but it is the adverb, YET.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that ferments sugar into alcohol in beer and wine.

clue.text: Quick examination, long ago accomplished

parts.note: once means at some time long past, as in 'once upon a time'
something accomplished is finished or over

explanation.surface: A brief check was completed a long time back.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a rapid look or inspection, a glance up and down.

clue.text: Almost overdue, going by way of the country

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for overdue is dropped

parts.note: something overdue is late
via means passing through, by way of

explanation.surface: Running a little late, someone travels through the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic nation, one of the three Baltic states, so it is a country.

clue.text: One by one, the team appears

parts.note: the digit one set beside another digit one reads as the number 11

explanation.surface: The players come out one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One by one' looks like 'one at a time', but put a 1 beside a 1 and you get 11. A cricket or football side is called an eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has eleven players, so the side itself is called an eleven.

clue.text: Lamb, perhaps, to try before it's cooked

indicators.note: before places the attempt in front of the rearranged letters

parts.note: to essay something is to attempt or try it

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook trying out some lamb before it goes in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is Charles Lamb, the English writer of the Essays of Elia, not the meat. 'cooked' turns ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was famous for his personal prose pieces, so he is an example of a writer of short pieces.
